header:
Date: 2027-05-10
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Redwood CSM), Marco Li (Redwood Support), Maya Rodriguez (Pinegate Head of MLOps), Evan Cho (CTO), Lisa Nguyen (Security Lead), Tom Harper (PM), Rina Patel (SRE)
summary: Onboarding kickoff for Pinegate Health. Intro to Redwood product surface, confirmation of security and deployment constraints (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreement to run baseline benchmarks and provide prompt sets. Agreed weekly check-ins and next steps for sharing docs and scheduling technical deep dive.
topics: Pinegate current infra and constraints (VPC, on-prem, data residency)
Redwood deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security & compliance: SOC2, ISO, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Technical deep dive & benchmarking plan (latency, throughput, cost)
Onboarding timeline, success criteria, and next steps
transcript: 00:00 Sophie Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Sophie from Redwood, I'm the AE working with Pinegate. 00:05 Daniel Kim: Hi all Daniel here I'm the solutions engineer I'll be leading the technical deep dive. 00:10 Maya Rodriguez: Thanks Sophie, Maya here, Head of MLOps at Pinegate, excited to get started. 00:15 Evan Cho: Evan CTO, quick context we have a mixed cloud on-prem footprint, low tolerance for PHI leakage and tight latency reqs. 00:25 Sophie Patel: Great that's super helpful, can you say a bit about current QPS and typical sequence lengths? 00:33 Maya Rodriguez: Sure, during peak we hit about 200 reqs per second for chat flows, average sequence around 512 tokens, some gen tasks up to 1024, we also use a caching layer in front of our microservices. 00:45 Daniel Kim: Okay good, that helps a lot. For those latency numbers are you targeting p95 under 300ms for user interactive flows? 00:54 Tom Harper: Yes p95 around 300-350ms would be ideal, cost is also a concern so we want balance. 01:02 Sophie Patel: Yep that's the typical tradeoff we help dial in - batching, KV prefix cache, quant profiles for cost-vs-latency. 01:15 Lisa Nguyen: On security side we need SSO (SAML 2.0), RBAC, KMS integration and audit logs, plus support for a private VPC or on-prem option. 01:27 Aisha Rahman: We can absolutely support all of those - Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC and integrates with KMS/HSM, and we provide audit logs and SAML SSO. 01:38 Evan Cho: Is SOC2 and ISO attestation available? I need to share that with procurement. 01:44 Sophie Patel: Yes we will send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, I'll include them in the onboarding packet. Apologies if the doc names get munged in the zip, sometimes the automation changes filenames. 01:55 Maya Rodriguez: Quick question about data retention, pinegate needs data-at-rest encryption and option for no-data-retention on hosted. 02:03 Marco Li: We offer configurable retention windows and a no-retention mode for hosted where payloads are not stored - for private deployments the customer controls retention. 02:14 Rina Patel: For VPC option do we get egress control and direct private peering? 02:20 Daniel Kim: Yes VPC peering and private endpoints are supported, we'll share network diagram later. 02:28 Tom Harper: On Dedicated vs Hosted, what are typical commit sizes and how does autoscaling behave? 02:36 Sophie Patel: Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with monthly/annual commits - autoscaling policies can be tuned, burst capacity is available for spikes. We'll share a pricing sheet and example commit tiers after this call. 02:47 Evan Cho: Also curious about model catalog - can we bring custom models or do we have to use Redwood-curated models? 02:54 Daniel Kim: You can deploy customer models in Private/Dedicated, and for Hosted we provide curated open models and variants; we also support pinned model versions to avoid drift. 03:05 Maya Rodriguez: For benchmarking we'd like to run our top 10 prompts across candidate model/quant combos. What's the SE workflow? 03:12 Daniel Kim: We'll schedule a benchmark session, we'll provision a test harness and run latency/cost per-token comparisons. We'll need prompt sets and traffic profile. 03:22 Sophie Patel: I'll follow up with a template for prompt submission, and Daniel will share the benchmark plan. 03:30 Lisa Nguyen: Also need to confirm KMS provider compatibility - we use AWS KMS and an HSM for some keys. 03:36 Marco Li: We support AWS KMS and can integrate with customer HSMs in Private deployments; we'll document the KMS flow. 03:46 Maya Rodriguez: One more - do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants on overload? 03:53 Daniel Kim: Yes we have rollout controls: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to keep apps online during capacity constraints. 04:02 Tom Harper: Great. Timeline wise we aim to be in a pilot within 4 weeks, production in 8-10 weeks, assuming no major network/security blockers. Is that feasible? 04:12 Sophie Patel: Yes that aligns with typical onboarding - pilot in 3-6 weeks, prod in 6-12 depending on procurement and network setup. 04:20 Evan Cho: Procurement will need a pricing sheet and SOC2/ISO. 04:24 Sophie Patel: I'll send pricing examples and SOC2/ISO, and the onboarding packet. 04:30 Maya Rodriguez: Any blockers on the SE side to run the benchmark? 04:34 Daniel Kim: Need the prompt list and a staging endpoint access window; also if you want private deployment we'll need network peering details. 04:43 Maya Rodriguez: We'll compile prompts and share by Friday, and schedule the benchmark next week. 04:48 Aisha Rahman: We'll also set up the weekly check-in cadence; starting 2027-05-18 weekly 30m. 04:55 Lisa Nguyen: One security nuance - we require rotation schedule for keys and auditability for deletions. 05:01 Marco Li: Supported; we'll include key rotation recommendations and audit log examples in the docs. 05:10 Sophie Patel: Recap - Sophie will send onboarding pack + SOC2/ISO + pricing, Daniel will own benchmark and technical deep dive, Maya will provide prompt sets and traffic profile, Lisa will send compliance list, and Aisha will schedule weekly check-ins. 05:25 Evan Cho: Sounds good, thanks everyone. 05:30 Sophie Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and next steps. 05:35 [Call ends] Note: transcription contains some ASR errors, product names occasionally mangled (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" transcribed as "Redwood dedicate"), and slight speaker overlap in a few spots.
notes: Customer requires no-data-retention option for hosted and VPC/on-prem for PHI workloads
Agreement to run benchmark on top 10 prompts across model/quant variants
Procurement needs SOC2/ISO and pricing examples
Weekly 30m check-ins to be scheduled starting 2027-05-18
